# National Survey on Drug Use and Health (NSDUH): agent index

SAMHSA's annual survey of substance use, mental health and treatment in the civilian, noninstitutionalized population aged 12 and older, conducted by RTI International. Annual public use files.

Publisher: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), Center for Behavioral Health Statistics and Quality. Dataset id: `nsduh`. Records follow PublicDataToolkit standard 0.1.

Terms: https://www.samhsa.gov/data/data-we-collect/nsduh-national-survey-drug-use-and-health/datafiles. LLM processing: `allowed`.

Dimensions: `wave` is the year.

## How the shards are organized

Every shard is the result of a filter over the records, and its header says which filter and what completeness label it supports. Each shard comes in two forms with the same variables: `.txt`, one line per variable, for scanning; and `.jsonl`, the records with corrections applied, for details. The first JSONL line is the shard's header (`{"shard": ...}`); every later line is a variable. A shard too big to read at once (about 20,000 tokens) is split into parts.

The JSONL records are compact: `availability` maps each form (or `all`) to runs of waves, `origins` gives where each field came from as `kind:source` or `rule:name@version`, and `origins.codes` is the origin the codes share (a code lists its own when they differ). Per-wave counts and the notes on origins are left out. The full records in `metadata/` are canonical; each shard header's `full_records` names the files.

Line form: `name | waves by form | scale signature | label | question text`. A run like `1972-1978` means every wave of the release in that span. `1972-1985,1987-2024 (not 1986)` means the release has a 1986 wave and the variable wasn't in it. `all 1972-1987; form A,C 1988-2024` means everyone was asked through 1987 and only forms A and C from 1988. The release's waves are: `2023`: 2023; `2024`: 2024; `2025`: 2025. A trailing `*` on a name means a field was corrected.

`SKILL.md` says how to label an answer drawn from these files.

A change of meaning (codes, wording or universe) gives a second line, marked ↳, under the first.
